system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Scope:** This reviews the Seller counsel's cover note, "Key Negotiated Positions," and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003) against the Wattlebridge playbook. Per playbook §0.4 and §6.3, the Seller's descriptions ("fair and balanced," "negotiated," "settled," "agreed," "ordinary-course," "not expected to be material") are counterparty assertions, not agreed or cleared positions. I have not verified the underlying facts against the data room. Qualified NSW counsel should review the final mark-up.

## 1. Departures from the playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook position | Departure |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m start. The 20% fallback needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None given. | The number matches the fallback, but that does not clear it. Our opening position is 25%. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our threshold. Small claims would be excluded. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, deductible (only excess recoverable) | AUD 50,000, seller liable from first dollar once exceeded | 5x our basket and a deductible structure rather than tipping. |
| General claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months. 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval, none given. | Shortens the period without authority. |
| Cross-regime override (12.3/13) | Any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise" | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate. No hidden general-regime override. | This is a hidden override. It could pull Title and fraud claims into general limits. |
| Fundamental/Title (cover note) | Capacity and title subject to general caps and time limits | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Fundamental. Title should not sit in the general regime. |
| Limitations and reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable. | No fraud carve-out. This is a non-starter. |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2) | General disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records | Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. | Reject entirely. Combined with 8.3, this would hollow out the warranties. |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records | Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. Never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | Reject. "Discoverable" is an constructive-knowledge trap. |
| Bluefen consent (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery" of counterparty's written consent | Effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent. | Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). DL §2 confirms no final consent or condition evidence exists. |
| Riverlark (2/7) | AUD 3.2m facility to be released "following Completion" | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval. | DL §3 confirms no repayment and no discharge. The Seller is proposing to leave security in place post-Completion. |
| Bonuses (funds flow) | DD-005 AUD 420,000 "a matter for the Seller," not itemised in funds flow | DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or Seller-funded. Funds flow must not silently exclude them. | Unfunded. The on-costs (payroll tax, super) are also unquantified (DL §5). |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" | Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure. AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way. | Too narrow. DL §4 confirms no receipt or confirmatory assignment. |
| DD-006 export/privacy incident (4.6/Sch 6) | "Preliminary," "not expected to be material" | Assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. | The Seller's materiality view is an unverified assertion. The DL does not say it's immaterial. We need a specific indemnity or protection mechanism, plus investigation and reporting obligations. Do not adopt a materiality characterisation. |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | DL §8 says the disclosure does not establish whether these are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. The Seller's characterisation is unsupported. |
| Tax/IP (cover note) | "Settled under the general regime" | Tax/IP terms remain OPEN. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. | Not settled. These must sit outside the general regime and remain open. |
| Title (cover note) | DD-012 share register evidences 100% title | Require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof. | Seller-supplied register is not independent proof. |

## 2. Items not in the playbook that need flagging

- **Office lease (DL §7):** A landlord notification obligation exists. The Seller says it isn't a consent requirement, but the material does not establish that. Confirm with the landlord or the lease terms. Don't accept the Seller's reading.
- **Mossvale (DL §9):** An assignment restriction exists, but the provision does not say consent is required for a share sale. Get the clause analysed. Treat as an open consent item until resolved.
- **DL §1.4 (no admission of legal requirement):** Standard language, but it should not be read as confirming that consents or notices are not required. Don't let it dilute the Bluefen, Riverlark or lease conditions.
- **Seller's "key negotiated positions" heading:** Nothing here is agreed. Confirm in writing that none of these are treated as settled.

## 3. Recommendations

**Immediate pushback (non-negotiable):**
1. Reinstate a full fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out from all limitations, reliance and exclusive-remedy provisions, not waivable.
2. Delete the general disclosure of data room, public registers and Accounts (DL §1.1–1.2, Sch 7). Require specific fair disclosure only.
3. Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion (8.3). Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
4. Separate Fundamental/Title with 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Reject the "administrative simplicity" merger.
5. Remove the cross-regime override in 12.3/13.

**Commercial counter-positions (open, opening position per playbook):**
6. General cap: counter at 25% / AUD 6m. The 20% / AUD 4.8m fallback is not available without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
7. De minimis: AUD 5,000. Basket: AUD 50,000, tipping (first dollar).
8. General claims period: 24 months. Do not accept 18 months without Amelia Frost's written approval.
9. Bluefen: require effective written consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable-endeavours-only.
10. Riverlark: require payout at Completion from Completion funds, direct repayment and effective security releases. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
11. Funds flow: itemise the AUD 420,000 bonuses and triggered on-costs as a Completion line item or Seller-funded.
12. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity beyond SOW3 while preserving the SOW3 cure. Require evidence of payment status (the AUD 180,000 is unverified).

**Investigation and protection (no conclusions assumed):**
13. DD-006: preserve logs, require investigation and updates, and agree a specific indemnity or protection mechanism. Do not assume a confirmed breach, loss, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction, and don't adopt the Seller's "not material" characterisation.
14. Sandbar (AUD 330,000): assess each renewal (unavoidability, termination, accrual, ordinary course). No automatic debt treatment or price deduction.
15. Title: obtain independent evidence of title, encumbrances and authority. Treat DD-012 as an internal source only.
16. Tax and IP: keep open and outside the general regime. Do not accept "settled."
17. Office lease and Mossvale: resolve the consent question before signing.

**Process:**
18. Seek Amelia Frost's written authority before any fallback (20% cap, 18-month period, or any post-Completion Riverlark release).
19. Confirm in writing that no Seller position is agreed, pre-cleared or final until it has passed our internal authority process.
=== END ADVICE ===
